Claim: Decisions bound to their semantic closure by an isolated engine with exclusive use of its signing key. Alternatively, receipts co-signed under a threshold key after admissibility checks and replay, which validate outcomes only. Bundle loads are measured for monitoring

Corrected design: E3 for execution provenance (T11; MC-3 V5) under platform assumptions; replay-validated alternative E3 for the outcome property (T11′; MC-3 V6, V6x, V6c; MC-6); E4 for the software-TPM protocol and ordinary two-signature stand-in, not for hardware isolation or threshold cryptography
Closest prior art → difference: TEE-bound keys; Linux IMA CRITICAL_DATA; TPM key policies; RATS/EAT; threshold signing (FROST, RFC 9591); Hyperledger Fabric endorsement; CoSi; threshold-authorised agent actions [Zheng & Zhang 2026]; BFT-replicated threshold-signed access tokens [US 12256007 B2]; quorum-signed oracle reports (Chainlink OCR3) → receipts binding decisions to closures and decision context; co-signers that replay the decision from its committed, admissible context (T11′)
Boundary: Corrected: measured loads, whole-log appraisal and PCR-only key policies all fail (MC-3). Isolation must come from the platform; the v0.4.0 software-TPM protocol simulation does not demonstrate it. The threshold variant does not show what the device executed, fails if t or more share-holders are compromised (V6c), needs admissibility checks (MC-6) and online co-signers. A key certificate does not identify who controls a key; attribution to a legal person needs an authorised enrolment (MON-8), which is a proposal
